correctness.rationale: The all-real-parameter Cauchy–Binet formula and its derivative quadratic are derived explicitly. Endpoint values, strict convex quadratic root/sign positions and equality of the two endpoint determinants establish the globally unique interior maximizer precisely beyond the logarithmic-mean horizon. A derivative bound at 1/r proves every interior optimum occurs before the critical horizon. The threshold Taylor expansion and fixed-rate large-horizon limiting quadratic give the declared constants. The contained verifier actually passed 56,063 exact-rational and floating-point assertions, used only as supplemental checks; there are no computer-based infinite claims.

originality.rationale: Searches of primary full-text literature, published mathematical records, and recoverable earlier numerical-observability claims found no covering theorem for known distinct rates and three observation events with two pinned endpoints. The closest experimental article optimizes a different four-parameter objective numerically; the closest published sampling theorems concern rank, sensor subsets, or equally spaced multi-mode designs. The earlier confluent Jordan timing theorem is a singular rate-coalescence limit, not a theorem for arbitrary strictly distinct rates. The result is qualified by possible specialized older experimental-design coverage, including one abstract-only source. The logarithmic-mean constant occurs in Dette et al. (2004) for a different robust unknown-rate design; originality is assessed only for the complete pinned two-mode theorem, not the constant alone.
residual_risks: The full 1997 Dette–Neugebauer article was not accessed; its abstract is different but does not exclude an unexpected specialist corollary.
A different earlier exact-design theorem for two exponential basis functions and compulsory endpoint measurements could exist outside searched sources.
The full text behind the closest arithmetic-spectrum published summary was not accessible in the present review; its reported quantified problem is different.
Same-model scientific assessment and finite tests are not independent mathematical certification.

An old robust single-rate maximin design has the same log-mean formula; a stronger cross-model reformulation could in principle cover the new design if established, but the compared Fisher matrices and objectives differ.

value.rationale: The unknown initial amplitudes of two distinct known decays with compulsory initial/terminal observations form a naturally motivated minimal observability design for decay spectroscopy and dynamic sensing. The all-rate exact critical horizon, unique analytic timing law, nonmonotone timing response to longer horizons, and unbounded quantified information loss from endpoint repetition are structural, nontrivial decision boundaries. The setting is deliberately limited to a three-event determinant criterion, avoiding unsupported claims about general multi-exponential design.
